terms.comment: Our phrase: ēmptiō, a buying (Lewis & Short), with Traupman’s adjective interrētiālis, as in situs interrētiālis (website, Traupman 262). No reference work has a term for online shopping.

phrases.latin: Calceōs novōs per interrēte ēmī; crās afferentur.
phrases.english: I bought new shoes online; they’ll be delivered tomorrow.
Add this book to the basket.

phrases.latin: Calceōs in carrulum conjēcī; nunc solvendum est.
phrases.english: I’ve put the shoes in the basket; now I have to pay.

sources: Lewis & Short: emo · Lewis & Short: emptio · Lewis & Short: carrulus · Lewis & Short: conicio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261–262.
